column1: # Primary-language vectors. Shared by the corelib dictionary test
# (Dictionary::primary_lang) and the importers' tests (correctiond-import-cookbook), so the Rust and
# Format: a line "[en]", "[tl]" or "[war]" starts a lexicon section, read with
# the normal lexicon parser (word<TAB>count; repeated words are summed). A line
# "[expect]" starts the expectations: word<TAB>language, where language is
# en, tl, war, or none for a word in no lexicon. Lexicons load in the order
# en, tl, war (LangId 0, 1, 2). Lines starting with # are comments.
# Totals: en 10000, tl 1000, war 500, so per-million frequency is count*100 in
# en, count*1000 in tl and count*2000 in war.
# only in war, written capitalized in its lexicon
# three-way tie (10000 per million each): the first language, en, wins
# tl/war tie (50000 each): tl, listed before war, wins
# en/tl shared: fewer raw counts in tl (50 vs 400) but higher per million (50000 vs 40000)
# tl/war shared: fewer raw counts in war (15 vs 20) but higher per million (30000 vs 20000)
# repeated tl entry summed (10 -> 10000) beats war 4 (8000); unsummed (5000) would lose
